description:
Meet WildBananaMilkTea! 🍌🧋 We’re taking our curiosity beyond Earth with GhostPilot, a health-monitoring companion that introduces astronauts to a familiar face: their past self.

Our recipe brings together NASA research, an interactive body map and personal health comparisons to help astronauts spot changes and know what to check next. Add a generous splash of imagination, and that’s us! We are exploring how good design can make looking after yourself a little easier, even far from home.
summary:
GhostPilot is an offline web app that helps astronauts on long missions check their own health and decide what to do next. A 3D human body, posed the way bodies float in zero-g, is the way in. Tap a region to open short, timed checks linked to NASA's 17 named spaceflight health risks and its five hazards. The checks include an attention task, sleep and mood ratings, symptom reports, heart rate, a letter-chart eye test and on-device camera checks of shoulder movement and body shape.

Every check explains how to take it and why it matters. Each result is compared with the astronaut's own earlier readings (their "ghost") rather than population norms. Anything off turns the region red and comes with plain next steps: Watch, Tell surgeon or Act now. Once a day, a report is saved for the medical team to send via Hand Off at the next communication window. Real NASA ISS radiation and cabin-air data appear as mission context.

On the way to Mars, a message to the ground can take 20 minutes. GhostPilot helps crews notice changes early and act on them, without hiding what can't be measured onboard.
details:
GhostPilot helps astronauts answer three questions: How am I doing? What has changed? What should I do next? It is an offline-first health-monitoring prototype designed for long missions where medical support from Earth may be delayed or unavailable.

Astronauts navigate an interactive 3D body to complete guided checks for physical and mental wellbeing, including sleep, mood, attention, heart rate and movement. Each check explains how to take the measurement and why it matters. Results are compared with the astronaut’s own historical baseline, aka their “ghost”, to highlight changes and suggest next steps. A daily report gathers findings, concerns and missing measurements for export to the medical team.

Our creative approach combines a personal baseline, a clickable body map and a visual style inspired by crew procedure cards. An optional camera scan fits the avatar’s proportions and estimates thigh breadth for tracking. NASA’s Human Research Program informs the checks, its Human Integration Design Handbook informs the body illustration, and archived ISS environmental data provides clearly labelled mission context.

We built GhostPilot with React, TypeScript, Vite, Three.js, Blender, MediaPipe and Recharts. Camera processing runs on the device, while IndexedDB and a service worker support local storage and offline use after the initial load. Playwright and axe-core support browser and accessibility testing.

We considered limited crew time, equipment availability, communication delays, privacy, accessibility and measurement uncertainty. Our intended impact is to help astronauts recognize changes, take informed next steps and share clearer information with medical teams. The approach could also benefit remote communities and isolated workers on Earth. GhostPilot remains a prototype; clinical guidance and camera measurements require further validation.
